newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena CEO sees bright future for smaller hubs.
newsitem.headline: Sabena CEO sees bright future for smaller hubs.

text.p: Paul Reutlinger, chief executive of Belgian airline Sabena, said on Tuesday that airports such as Brussels, Zurich and Vienna would benefit from congestion which was bound to hit the major European hubs.
Reutlinger told a meeting of the European Aviation Club that one of Sabena's key goals was to cut the connecting time between two flights via Brussels to 27 minutes from 35 now.
He noted that Vienna had an average connecting time, with baggage, of just 25 minutes.
"This is an important element for secondary airports and hubs in Europe to compete against the mega-hubs," he said.

"The mega-hubs (London, Paris, Frankfurt) in the long run are going to be like dinosaurs, getting bigger and fatter until they are not operational any more, and this will be the chance for airports like Brussels, Zurich or Vienna to be really competitive," Reutlinger said.
